# ROI what-if — "Shopify app block for embedding reco widgets / inline blocks"

**Generated by `/support-roi` (read-only over the registry). 14 windows W16–W29 (2026-04-13 → 2026-07-13). Omega shard = lower bound.**

## The dev effort being evaluated

Ship a **Shopify theme app extension (app block / app embed)** so merchants place Maestra reco widgets and inline blocks into their theme via the Shopify theme editor — a native, reserved slot — instead of today's placement hacks: CSS-selector "replace content", per-widget `on_render` JS to strip conflicting site markup, and hand-installed `theme.liquid` tracker snippets.

**Scope:** this fixes **where/how the widget mounts**, not what it renders. Template/markup and visual-CSS gaps are explicitly out of scope (see below).

## Toil this would remove — 14 weeks (H1 2026)

| | Tickets | % of support toil | Mechanics |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Placement family** (this effort) | **10 / 92** | **11%** | ~45 theme-slot custom-code mechanics |

Confirmed cause→effort mapping (Strong only):

| Cause | Group | Tickets | Why the app block resolves it |
|---|---|--:|---|
| `rc-mf-reco-theme-slot-injection` | Missing feature | 3 | Bullseye — a native theme-aware slot *is* the missing feature (Shopify section / cart drawer / header placement). Also ~45 custom-code mechanics that hand-place widgets. |
| `rc-bug-reco-replace-content-race` | Bug | 5 | The A/B "replace content" race and the add-to-cart / cart-update render race both stem from replacing arbitrary page DOM; a reserved app-block slot removes the replace mechanism, so nothing to race. |
| `rc-cc-legacy-tracker-per-theme-layout` | Custom code | 2 | Manual `theme.liquid` tracker installs that break per theme / after rename → replaced by the app embed. This exact fix ("switch to app embed") was already used once. |

## Explicitly NOT credited

- `rc-cc-popup-inline-template-gap` (3t / **424 mechanics**, the biggest custom-code bucket) and the reco visual/markup causes (`rc-mf-reco-variant-dedup`, `rc-mf-reco-widget-visual-customization`) — these are **template/CSS gaps** (what the widget renders), which an app block does not fill. Don't conflate "embed it natively" with "author its markup."
- **Partial, deliberately excluded** (would add ~2 tickets + a large non-placement mechanics tail): `rc-cc-dom-dependent-targeting-breaks` (visibility JS reacting to storefront events still needs DOM hooks) and `rc-cc-popup-integration-ops` (211m, but mostly API/form ops unrelated to embedding). If the app block also exposes native add-to-cart / product context, revisit these.

## Assumptions & caveats

- **Omega shard only → lower bound;** true figures higher across shards, and only the 14 run weeks are counted.
- **Coverage < 100%.** A native slot is high-coverage for these three causes but not total — A/B testing two variants in one slot still needs the app to swap content (app-controlled, not a DOM race), and some legacy themes resist app embeds. Assume ~80–85% realistic removal → **~8–9 of the 10 tickets**.
- Placement mechanics (45, theme-slot slice) overlap other custom-code buckets — don't sum them with template-gap/integration figures.

## Bottom line

A Shopify app block is a **focused, ~11%-of-toil** win that removes an entire *class* of placement toil — the fragile replace-content/DOM-selector/manual-tracker pattern — and its footprint is **growing** (peak in the latest week). It is **not** the largest single lever (the reco self-serve + template-gap families remain bigger), but it is clean, well-scoped, and eliminates a recurring source of both bug tickets and hand-authored placement code. Best sequenced alongside — not instead of — the reco template/markup self-serve work.
